target_customer: Indian college students and young professionals who want job-ready tech skills and placement
problem: Online course completion rates are low and Indian graduates often lack employability, so Edyst pairs peer-to-peer learning with placement.
business_model: Paid learning programs for students with placement outcomes, per company claims of a 50 percent placement ratio
product_category: Online coding learning and employability platform

founders.name: Srinivas Sriramdas
prior_employers: Deloitte Australia and India (Head of Marketing Communications and Business Development)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has over 20 years in marketing, business development, strategy and operations. A Seedtable page quoting EdSurge names a co-founder Vasu Sriramdas, not confirmed from a primary source so not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: An online learning platform with peer features and course delivery is standard web engineering, with the hard part being content and outcomes rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Content and learning platforms are easy to copy, and defensibility rests only on placement relationships and community, none evidenced in the sources.

incumbents: Large Indian and global online course providers
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on incumbent actions toward Edyst.

market_need_then: Edyst claims its course completion beats the industry average by 8x, and TechCrunch's W19 Demo Day roundup (seen only as a search summary) described it as a coding bootcamp for Indian college students seeking jobs.

branding.domain_note: Uses edyst.com, an exact .com (source: company site URL).

identity.voice_and_tone: recruiting copy calls for mavericks who love challenges and puzzles

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found beyond directory listings.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand was found, and name searches return unrelated Edyoucated and Edit style brands.

outcome_analysis: Edyst is listed as active with 11 people and claims strong completion and placement metrics, but no funding beyond a YC date of March 2019 and no later news was found. No shutdown, acquisition or layoffs were found either, so the story is unknown and small rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: Company website returned 503 so only the YC page and the long description were used. Funding: Seedtable lists a last funding date of 2019-03-18 with no amount, probably the YC deal, so no round is recorded. Competitor list is empty because searches returned no sources dated near the 2019 batch. A Persana blog says founded 2016, which conflicts with the YC page 2019 and is a low quality source. Co-founder Vasu Sriramdas appears only in a second-hand quote. Education of the founder not found.
